newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank strike not seen hurting India RBI auctions.
newsitem.headline: Bank strike not seen hurting India RBI auctions.

text.p: A countrywide strike of bank employees is unlikely to disrupt auctions held by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) later on Friday, dealers said.
"I don't think the strike will affect the auctions as treasuries are not participating (in the strike)," said a debt analyst at a securities firm in Bombay.
Most dealers expect the yield at the 91-day treasury bill to be more or less unchanged at 7.02 percent. The notified amount at Friday's auction is 3.0 billion rupees.
"At the last few auctions there was no difference between the actual cut-off and the weighted average," said Aashish Pitale, manager debt research at ICICI Securities and Finance.
This may not happen at Friday's auction as some participants may look forward to lower yields, following the example of Wednesday's 364-day treasury bill auction, he said.
At the 364-day treasury bill auction, the RBI cut the yield to 8.85 percent from the earlier 9.0 percent.
Most dealers expect the cut-off to be steady at 99.81 rupees at Friday's 14-day treasury bills auction.
An analyst at a debt research firm said the cut-off at Friday's repo auction could ease to 3.0 percent from 3.95.
But the amount of subscription could be lower, dealers said.
"About 17.0 billion rupees is maturing (from the previous repo)," said a dealer. "I don't see all of it being rolled over," he said.
